assessment.nobel_worthiness: The political-economy models of trade policy (protection for sale, lobbying, special interests) changed how economists and policymakers understand trade policy. The work is rigorous and has had broad influence across trade, political economy and public choice.
assessment.attribution: The Grossman-Helpman partnership is the clear core of this contribution. Helpman also appears in the firm-heterogeneity candidate (B020), but the joint political-economy work is a coherent, cleanly attributable pair.
assessment.maturity: The central results date from the 1990s and have had decades of confirmation, extension and empirical testing. No timing concern.
uncertainties: Empirical validation of the lobbying models is more mixed than their theoretical influence.
Trade has been recognised before (2008), which some may weigh against another trade award.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Formal and empirical analysis of how constitutions, electoral rules and state capacity shape fiscal policy and development. It is a foundational research program in modern political economics with wide influence.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are the central figures through their joint work on political economics. Besley's work on state capacity and accountability is closely linked and complementary. Three is the maximum, and the trio is coherent.
assessment.maturity: Developed over about 30 years and widely replicated and extended. The 2024 prize on institutions and prosperity adds a possible adjacency issue but also shows field-level recognition.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2024 institutions prize may be read as redundancy.
The relative contributions of the three are hard to apportion.
Possible Swedish-institutional proximity; disclosed here, not adjudicated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Credit cycles, collateral constraints and amplification of shocks. The 1997 model is a central workhorse of macro-finance, with strong theoretical and policy relevance after the 2008 crisis.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore are the clear originators of the collateral-constraint credit-cycle mechanism. Gertler and Gilchrist belong to the adjacent financial-accelerator tradition, and Bernanke is already a laureate, so a two-person ballot is cleanest.
assessment.maturity: The work has stood for nearly 30 years and its influence on research and central banking is well documented.
uncertainties: Prior crisis-related recognition (2022) could affect committee appetite.
The boundary between this and the financial-accelerator credit may be disputed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantile regression is a general tool for analysing distributional effects, now standard in applied work across economics and other sciences. It has substantial methodological and practical impact.
assessment.attribution: The 1978 Koenker-Bassett paper is the founding contribution and Koenker led its development. Chernozhukov's later contributions (inference, distributional methods) are significant but are also credited in B007. Keeping the ballot to the originators gives a more attributable pair.
assessment.maturity: More than 45 years of use and theoretical development. The contribution is fully mature.
uncertainties: Econometrics has been recognised relatively recently (2021), which may reduce committee appetite.
Whether the committee prefers to include Chernozhukov is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The alternating-offers bargaining model and its market extension give a tractable non-cooperative foundation for bargaining and decentralised trade. It underpins work in labour, search and market-design theory. It is a canonical result in game theory.
assessment.attribution: Rubinstein (1982) is the originator of the alternating-offers solution. Rubinstein-Wolinsky (1985) extends it to markets with frictions. Binmore's contributions (the Nash program, 1986 work) are real but more supporting, so he is omitted.
assessment.maturity: More than 40 years of established influence and wide use in textbooks and applied theory.
uncertainties: Game theory has been recognised several times, so the committee may judge this area saturated.
Whether Binmore should share credit is a legitimate question.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic panel GMM estimators (Arellano-Bond, Arellano-Bover, Blundell-Bond) are among the most widely used econometric tools in applied microeconomics and macroeconomics. Their practical influence is very large.
assessment.attribution: The Arellano-Bond and Blundell-Bond papers are the key estimators, so the credited trio is reasonable. Blundell also appears in B037, and the structural labour-supply work is a distinct contribution.
assessment.maturity: The core papers date from 1991-1998 and have been used extensively for decades.
uncertainties: Methodological tools are sometimes judged below conceptual advances in the prize's history.
Known weaknesses such as instrument proliferation may temper the assessment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Combines the task-based view of technology with trade-shock evidence to explain labour-demand change, job polarisation and local labour-market adjustment. It has had very high academic and policy influence.
assessment.attribution: Autor is the central figure. The China-shock evidence is jointly Autor-Dorn-Hanson, and Katz's contribution is the earlier skill-premium and task work. The proposed trio reflects the China-shock core, and attribution to Katz is a genuine alternative.
assessment.maturity: Core papers from 2003-2013 have been widely replicated and debated. It is reasonably mature, though interpretation continues to evolve.
uncertainties: The magnitude and persistence of the China shock are debated in the literature.
The attribution split between the task framework and trade-shock work is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Large-scale administrative data on intergenerational mobility and neighbourhood effects have reshaped both measurement and policy debate on opportunity. The methodological and empirical contribution is substantial.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is the clear leader, with Hendren and Friedman as principal co-authors. Katz is credited for the Moving to Opportunity work but would exceed the three-name limit.
assessment.maturity: The work is more recent (largely 2014 onward). Its influence is clear, but some findings on causal neighbourhood effects are still under scrutiny.
uncertainties: The relatively short time since the key results.
The committee may judge it premature relative to older candidates.
Credit division with Katz and others is complex.
